title: Debian Packages job fails - runner OutOfMemoryException during apt-get install inside Docker container
signature: system outofmemoryexception was thrown during debian packages docker container step|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Debian Packages / Debian Packages
failed_jobs.symptom: Step 'Install debian packages & check conflicts' aborted with a .NET System.OutOfMemoryException raised by the Actions runner host while apt-get was retrying delayed downloads of libexpat1 from azure.archive.ubuntu.com.

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status

##[error]Exception of type 'System.OutOfMemoryException' was thrown.
Stop and remove container: 38eb2c1e14fd49b3a15bfd671f34c336_openvinogithubactionsazurecriodockerhububuntu2204_92bc69
root_cause: The 'Install debian packages & check conflicts' step ran apt-get inside a Docker container on the Actions runner. apt-get repeatedly failed to fetch libexpat1 from azure.archive.ubuntu.com's delayed-download queue, logging hundreds of near-identical 'W: Tried to start delayed item ... but failed' warnings within milliseconds of each other. This warning storm, combined with process/log buffering inside the GitHub Actions runner's Docker step host process, exhausted available memory and the .NET runner process threw a System.OutOfMemoryException, aborting the step and forcing a container teardown. The underlying trigger is a flaky/degraded mirror connection to azure.archive.ubuntu.com (consistent with several prior Network-category patterns for this same job), but the fatal symptom here is the runner host's own OutOfMemoryException rather than a clean apt-get failure, so it is tracked as an Infrastructure issue distinct from the existing Network patterns.
reproduction_steps: N/A - failure is tied to GitHub Actions runner/container resource behavior when the apt mirror stalls; not reliably reproducible locally. To approximate: run `apt-get install openvino` in the same ubuntu:22.04 container image while throttling/blocking outbound access to azure.archive.ubuntu.com and observe repeated delayed-item retries.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed 'Debian Packages' job; this is a transient infrastructure/network condition, not a code defect in PR #37274.

Consider lowering apt's Acquire::Retries or adding a shorter per-item timeout in the workflow's apt configuration to fail fast instead of looping on delayed items until the runner process exhausts memory.
Monitor whether azure.archive.ubuntu.com mirror instability recurs; if it does, consider pointing the Debian Packages job at an alternate/cached apt mirror.
prevention_strategies: Add a bounded timeout/retry budget around apt-get invocations in the Debian Packages job so a slow/flaky mirror surfaces as a clean apt failure (fail-fast) instead of an unbounded retry loop that can exhaust the runner container's memory. Consider capturing apt output to a size-capped log file rather than letting thousands of near-duplicate warnings stream to the Actions log/host process.
historical_context: Multiple prior investigations recorded Network-category failures for this same job (apt-get unable to connect to azure.archive.ubuntu.com, timeouts/refused connections; see patterns 7d2e2ff59d37c6b4 count=9, 7d52cc57d8ed2a36, 98edf6d4fbc865bd, a3d456bd40bd9f42, c8d00529252cfb02, e65acb49deb19d88). This is the first occurrence where the failure manifested as a runner-level System.OutOfMemoryException rather than an apt-level connection error, so it is recorded as a new, related but distinct Infrastructure pattern.
